title: Advancing 4D STEM Using Computational Techniques
content: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) is a state-of-the-art method for collecting transmitted scattering events in a STEM. Unlike integrating radial detectors, the full diffraction pattern is imaged in the far-field for each probe position, allowing momentum resolution of the transmitted electrons. Using these diffraction patterns, a variety of different computational methods can be employed to analyze the specimen, such as applying a virtual detector, calculating the center of mass, or retrieving the phase shift induced by the object [1].
